frictionSummary: Developer portal access is now pay-per-use by default — no free tier for new developers.
prerequisites: An X account and a project created at console.x.com (the current developer console — some older guides still point to developer.x.com)
A payment method: since Feb 2026, new developers default to a pay-per-use model with no free tier
A clear estimate of call volume — pay-per-use is capped at 2M post reads/month even after buying credits

steps.title: Create a project and app in the developer console
steps.body: console.x.com → create a project, then an app inside it. Pick the app type: Web App or Automated App/Bot (confidential clients using a client secret) vs Native/Single-page app (public clients using PKCE only, no secret).

steps.title: Set up billing
steps.body: New developer accounts are pay-per-use by default: buy credits in the console (roughly $0.005 per post read, $0.01 per post created), with a hard cap of 2M post reads/month. Fixed Basic ($200/mo) and Pro ($5,000/mo) tiers still exist but are only available to developers already subscribed to them — new signups don't get the option.

steps.title: Configure OAuth 2.0 and generate credentials
steps.body: OAuth 2.0 is the recommended flow for new projects and is required for X API v2 user-context endpoints. Credentials are shown once in the console — save them immediately.
steps.codeSnippet:
curl -X POST https://api.twitter.com/2/oauth2/token \
  -d grant_type=authorization_code \
  -d client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID \
  -d redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI \
  -d code=THE_AUTH_CODE \
  -d code_verifier=YOUR_PKCE_VERIFIER

steps.title: Match the callback URL exactly
steps.body: A mismatched redirect URI, including a missing trailing path, is a common cause of failed connections — register it exactly as your app will send it.

scopes.grants: Create posts on the user's behalf
Obtain a refresh token for long-lived access

approval.expectedWait: No manual review to get started, but cost is the real gate — pay-per-use is the only on-ramp for new developers as of Feb 2026
approval.notes: Doc-sourced. There's no formal app-review queue like LinkedIn's, but new developers can no longer self-serve into a free tier — a payment method and credit purchase are required before the API is usable at all.

gotchas: No free tier for new developers since Feb 2026 — pay-per-use (credits) is the default, with Basic/Pro fixed tiers closed to new signups
Pay-per-use is capped at 2M post reads/month even with unlimited credit spend
App type matters for the OAuth flow: Web App / Automated App are confidential clients (client secret); Native / single-page apps are public clients (PKCE only, no secret)
Exact redirect URI matching is strict — a missing trailing slash or path segment breaks the callback
Some third-party tutorials still reference developer.x.com and a free tier — the current console is console.x.com and the free tier is gone for new accounts

do: Install twitter-api-v2 (Node) for OAuth 2.0 + API calls
Create /api/auth/twitter/callback — exchanges the code with PKCE at https://api.twitter.com/2/oauth2/token
Add placeholder env vars: TWITTER_CLIENT_ID, TWITTER_CLIENT_SECRET, TWITTER_REDIRECT_URI
Wire up a "Connect X" button redirecting to https://twitter.com/i/oauth2/authorize with scope=tweet.read%20tweet.write%20users.read%20offline.access and a PKCE code_challenge
Store the refresh token (offline.access) since access tokens are short-lived
dont: Set up billing or buy API credits — that's a real cost decision for the developer to make
Enter the real client secret anywhere — leave it as an env placeholder
Assume a free tier is available — budget for pay-per-use or a fixed tier before building against this API
